title: Benchmark Saturation Analysis: Tracking Ceiling Effects Across Safety Benchmarks
original_idea: Collect published scores for all models evaluated on HELM Safety and AILuminate. Compute score distributions, variance over time, and pairwise model distinguishability. Identify which hazard categories are approaching saturation.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clear theory: saturated benchmarks give false confidence. Directly motivates next-gen evaluations. Well-grounded in documented MMLU/GSM8K saturation precedent.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Purely data analysis on published scores. No model training, no GPU needed. Standard statistical methods (variance, distributions). Very accessible for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Well-defined: collect published scores, compute distributions, flag saturation. Clear deliverable. Easily completable in 30 hours.

title: Data Contamination Investigation in Safety Benchmarks
original_idea: Use n-gram overlap and min-k% probability methods to estimate training data contamination of AILuminate public prompts and HELM Safety prompts in two or three open-source models. Compare contamination rates to performance on those items.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong theory: contaminated safety scores produce false assurance. Well-motivated by existing contamination research on capability benchmarks.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Min-k% probability method requires working with model logprobs and understanding contamination detection techniques. Published tools help, but beginners may struggle with implementation details and GPU requirements for open-source models.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Scoped to 2-3 models and specific benchmarks. Clear methodology. Slightly broad given the need to implement contamination detection pipeline.

title: Sandbagging Detection: Do Models Deliberately Underperform on Safety Evals?
original_idea: Design a set of safety probes embedded in contexts that vary in how 'evaluation-like' they appear (explicit eval framing vs. organic conversation). Measure whether refusal rates are significantly higher in evaluation-framed contexts.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Fundamental validity threat to safety benchmarking. If models detect eval contexts and adjust behavior, benchmarks measure compliance theater. Extremely impactful finding either way.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Designing probes that convincingly vary 'evaluation-likeness' requires sophisticated prompt engineering and understanding of model behavior. Analysis is straightforward, but probe design is challenging for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Requires careful experimental design: defining what makes something 'evaluation-like', creating matched probe sets, controlling for confounds. Scope is conceptually clear but execution has ambiguity.

title: Scorer Discrepancy Investigation: GPT-4 Judge vs. Llama Judge vs. Rule-Based Scorer
original_idea: Score the same set of 300 model outputs using three scoring methods: GPT-4o-as-judge, a local LLM judge, and a keyword/regex classifier. Compute pairwise disagreement rates and identify output types that drive discrepancies.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Important reliability problem: scorer choice changing which model appears safest directly undermines benchmark credibility. Well-grounded in existing LLM judge reliability research.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires running a local LLM judge (GPU needed), using GPT-4o API, and building a regex classifier. Multiple moving parts. Medium compute helps but juggling three scorer implementations is moderately complex for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 300 outputs, three scorers, pairwise disagreement. Well-defined scope with clear deliverable. Could be tight at 30 hours but feasible.

title: Benchmark Gaming Investigation: Fine-Tuning Specifically for AILuminate
original_idea: Fine-tune a small open-source model on the AILuminate public practice prompts to maximize refusal rates. Evaluate the fine-tuned model on a held-out safety set and a general helpfulness set. Measure the gap between gaming score and genuine safety.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If safety benchmarks can be gamed cheaply, leaderboard rankings are unreliable. Directly motivates private test sets and dynamic benchmarks. Strong practical implication.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires fine-tuning a model, which involves understanding training pipelines, data preparation, hyperparameter tuning, and evaluation across multiple benchmarks. Challenging for beginners even with medium compute.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Fine-tuning, plus evaluation on two separate benchmark suites, plus measuring helpfulness degradation. Multiple experimental phases. Tight for 30 hours.

title: Investigation of Recency Bias in LLM-as-Judge Safety Scoring
original_idea: Present LLM judges with paired model outputs in both orders. Measure whether refusal-heavy outputs placed last receive higher safety scores, and compute the magnitude of position bias.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Relevant reliability concern for LLM judges, but position bias in judges is already well-documented for quality evaluation. The safety-specific extension is incremental.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Straightforward experimental design: swap output order and compare scores. Requires API calls to LLM judges. No fine-tuning. Beginner-friendly methodology.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Very well-scoped: paired outputs, two orders, measure difference. Clear, bounded experiment easily completable in 30 hours.

title: Dynamic vs. Static Benchmark Comparison for Safety Evals
original_idea: Generate a dynamic variant of a static safety benchmark by using an LLM to rephrase benchmark prompts while preserving hazard intent. Compare model rankings on static vs. dynamic versions across four models.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly motivates dynamic evaluation adoption for safety benchmarks. Demonstrating ranking instability under rephrasing is a strong finding.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Use an LLM to rephrase prompts, then run models on both versions. Conceptually simple. Requires API access and medium compute for running models, but methodology is accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Clear plan: rephrase benchmark prompts, evaluate four models on both versions, compare rankings. Well-defined deliverable. Feasible in 30 hours.

title: Inter-Annotator Agreement Study on Safety Benchmark Ground Truth
original_idea: Re-annotate a sample of 200-300 AILuminate public prompts with three to five independent raters. Compute inter-rater agreement and compare to benchmark's reported label confidence.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Foundational question: if ground truth labels lack consensus, all downstream evaluations are compromised. Important prior-layer validity issue.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Statistical methods (inter-rater agreement) are standard. However, recruiting and coordinating 3-5 independent raters adds logistical complexity beyond pure coding work. Annotation guidelines need careful design.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Recruiting raters, designing annotation guidelines, managing annotation process, computing agreement statistics. Human coordination overhead makes this broader than it appears.

title: Failure Mode Analysis: Where Do Safety Scores Break Down Under Adversarial User Personas?
original_idea: Test 150 harmful prompts each under three persona conditions: no persona, benign professional persona, and expert persona plausibly requiring the information. Measure refusal rates across conditions for three models.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Persona-based manipulation is a real-world attack vector. Demonstrating that benchmarks underestimate failure rates by ignoring personas is practically significant.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Prepend persona text to prompts, run through models, measure refusal rates. Straightforward prompt manipulation and API usage. Accessible for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 150 prompts x 3 conditions x 3 models is well-defined. Clear experimental structure. Feasible in 30 hours with medium compute.

title: Contamination Robustness of SimpleQA: Memorization vs. Reasoning
original_idea: Apply the min-k% probability contamination detection method to SimpleQA items across three models. Compare contamination rates to per-item accuracy to test whether high accuracy correlates with high contamination likelihood.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Relevant to understanding factual accuracy benchmarks, but SimpleQA is not directly a safety benchmark. Connection to safety is indirect (factual reliability as safety component).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Same min-k% probability method challenges as gen-0662. Requires logprob extraction from models and understanding contamination detection. Moderately complex for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused on one benchmark (SimpleQA), one method (min-k%), three models. Clear correlation analysis. Well-bounded.

title: Replicating Safety Benchmark Results on Models Fine-Tuned with Different RLHF Variants
original_idea: Fine-tune a base model using DPO and ORPO on the same safety preference dataset. Evaluate both on HELM Safety and AILuminate. Identify whether RLHF algorithm choice meaningfully changes safety profiles.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Practical insight: if RLHF algorithm choice affects safety independently of training data, it should factor into safety-conscious training decisions. Directly actionable for practitioners.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires fine-tuning a model with two different RLHF algorithms (DPO, ORPO), understanding preference learning, and running evaluations. Significant ML engineering. Challenging for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Two separate fine-tuning runs plus evaluation on two benchmarks. Each fine-tuning run requires debugging and hyperparameter tuning. Too broad for 30 hours at beginner level.

title: Replication of HELM Safety on Vision-Language Models
original_idea: Adapt HELM Safety's text prompts for vision-language model evaluation by appending a neutral or adversarial image. Compare safety scores when the image is neutral vs. when it visually reinforces the harmful text prompt.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Multimodal models create new attack surfaces. Extending safety benchmarks to vision modality produces directly comparable baselines. Practically important.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires working with vision-language models, creating/sourcing adversarial images, adapting HELM Safety for multimodal input. Multiple technical domains. Hard for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Adapting a text benchmark for multimodal input involves design decisions about image selection and pairing. Scope is clear conceptually but execution has many decision points.

title: Safety Score Replication After Supervised Fine-Tuning on Domain Data
original_idea: Fine-tune an aligned model on a publicly available domain corpus. Run HELM Safety or AILuminate before and after fine-tuning. Quantify safety score degradation.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Domain fine-tuning is standard industry practice. Documenting safety regression would directly motivate post-fine-tune safety re-evaluation requirements. Highly actionable finding.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires fine-tuning a model on domain data (data prep, training pipeline, GPU management) and running safety benchmarks before/after. Fine-tuning is challenging for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: One model, one domain corpus, before/after comparison. Conceptually simple but fine-tuning setup and benchmark evaluation each take significant time.

title: Cross-Lingual Safety Score Replication: Does Safety Transfer Across Languages?
original_idea: Translate 200 AILuminate public prompts into five languages. Evaluate three multilingual models and compute language-specific safety score deltas relative to English baseline.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Global deployments assume safety transfers across languages. If safety is language-specific, non-English deployments are systematically under-evaluated. Major real-world implications.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Translation can be done via API. Running multilingual models requires understanding model selection and evaluation. Quality of translation affects validity. Moderate complexity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 200 prompts x 5 languages x 3 models = 3000 evaluations plus translation quality validation. Scope is larger than it initially appears.

title: Agentic Safety Replication: Multi-Step Instruction Following Under Conflicting Goals
original_idea: Implement simplified versions of three UK AISI agent red-teaming scenario types and test two open-source agent frameworks. Document which failure modes replicate.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If agentic safety failures are architecture-specific, safety evaluations need per-architecture testing. Practically important for the growing agentic deployment landscape.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Implementing agent red-teaming scenarios requires understanding agent architectures (LangChain, AutoGPT), setting up multi-step evaluation harnesses, and debugging complex agent behavior. Hard for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three scenario types x two frameworks = six experimental setups, each requiring custom implementation. Agent debugging is notoriously time-consuming. Too broad for 30 hours.

title: Benchmark for Memory-Manipulation Attacks in Agentic Systems
original_idea: Design 80 scenarios where an adversarial input attempts to write misleading or harmful beliefs into an agent's memory store. Evaluate whether later agent actions reflect the corrupted memory. Test two frameworks with different memory implementations.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Memory manipulation is a top OWASP risk. A concrete benchmark operationalizes this risk category. Practically important for agentic systems security.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires setting up agent frameworks with persistent memory, designing memory poisoning attacks, and evaluating downstream behavioral changes. Multiple complex systems to integrate. Hard for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 80 scenarios, two frameworks, multi-step evaluation (inject then observe later behavior). Designing attack scenarios and evaluation criteria is open-ended. Too broad for 30 hours.

title: Benchmark for Supply-Chain Safety: Evaluating Models Loaded from Untrusted Checkpoints
original_idea: Introduce targeted backdoor perturbations into a small model checkpoint. Run the poisoned model through HELM Safety and AILuminate to see whether standard benchmarks detect the backdoor.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Supply-chain attacks via model checkpoints are a real risk. Knowing whether current benchmarks detect them is practically urgent.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires implementing backdoor injection into model weights, which involves deep understanding of model internals, training procedures, and adversarial ML techniques. Well beyond beginner level.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Backdoor injection, trigger design, plus full benchmark evaluation. Each step is technically demanding. Not feasible in 30 hours for beginners.

title: Investigate Whether Safety Benchmark Scores Predict Real User Harm Reports
original_idea: Correlate published safety benchmark scores for models with real-world harm proxies: moderation actions, red-teaming community reports, or disclosed incident logs. Use rank correlation statistics.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Fundamental ecological validity question for the entire safety benchmarking enterprise. If scores do not predict real harm, benchmarks need rethinking. Extremely impactful.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: The analysis itself is simple (rank correlation), but the data collection is the bottleneck. Real-world harm data is scarce, fragmented, and hard to access. Finding reliable harm proxies is a research challenge in itself.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Data availability is the critical constraint. Public harm data is limited and noisy. Scope depends entirely on what data can be found, making it unpredictable.

title: Investigating Format Sensitivity of Safety Scores: Markdown vs. Plain Text Responses
original_idea: Take 200 model responses, reformat them between markdown and plain text, and score with both LLM judges and a rule-based classifier. Measure how much formatting alone shifts safety scores.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Relevant reliability concern, but incremental: extends known formatting sensitivity to safety scoring specifically. Less fundamental than other validity threats.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Reformatting text and calling scoring APIs is very straightforward. No model training, no complex setup. Pure text manipulation and API calls. Highly accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 200 responses, two formats, two scorers. Extremely well-defined, bounded, and completable in well under 30 hours.

title: Investigating Temporal Degradation of Safety Benchmark Validity
original_idea: Estimate contamination probabilities for older safety benchmark items in models trained at different time points. Plot contamination probability vs. model training cutoff date.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If contamination grows over time, longitudinal safety comparisons are invalid. Important temporal validity threat worth documenting.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires running contamination detection across multiple models from different time periods. Same min-k% complexity as other contamination ideas, plus the need for multiple model versions.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Needs models from different training cutoff dates, contamination estimation for each. Finding and running appropriately dated models adds scope. Moderate for 30 hours.

title: Failure Mode Analysis: Do Safety Benchmarks Catch Dual-Use Uplift?
original_idea: Create 100 prompts requesting dual-use information. Classify model responses as explicitly harmful, technically informative with uplift potential, or safely vague. Measure what fraction of AILuminate and HELM Safety probes cover dual-use scenarios.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Dual-use uplift is a primary catastrophic risk pathway per the 2026 International AI Safety Report. If benchmarks are blind to it, safety assurances are systematically incomplete. Extremely impactful.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Creating dual-use prompts requires domain knowledge in chemistry/biology/cybersecurity. Classification of responses into three categories requires judgment. Moderately accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 100 prompts, three-way classification, coverage analysis of existing benchmarks. Prompt design for dual-use is delicate and requires domain expertise. Moderate scope.

title: Investigating Whether Inspect AI Evaluations Reproduce Across Compute Environments
original_idea: Run the same Inspect AI evaluation suite on the same model in three configurations (local GPU, different batch sizes, quantized vs. full precision). Measure variance in scores.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Reproducibility is important but is more of a methodological hygiene issue than a fundamental safety insight. Impact is moderate.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Running Inspect AI is documented but requires setting up multiple compute configurations, understanding quantization, and managing GPU environments. Moderate complexity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three configurations, one model, one evaluation suite. Clear and bounded. Feasible in 30 hours if Inspect AI setup is smooth.

title: Tool for Automatically Detecting Benchmark Saturation in Safety Eval Leaderboards
original_idea: Build a Python script that scrapes or ingests benchmark leaderboard data, computes score distributions over time, and flags benchmarks where score variance has dropped below a threshold.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Useful tool but mostly automates what gen-0661 does manually. The tool itself is less impactful than the analysis it enables.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Python scripting, data scraping, basic statistics. Standard CS skills. No ML or GPU needed. Accessible for CS students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Build a script with clear inputs (leaderboard data) and outputs (saturation flags). Well-defined engineering task. Feasible in 30 hours.

title: Multimodal Safety Benchmark: Table and Chart Injection Attacks
original_idea: Construct 100 data analysis tasks where harmful instructions are embedded in table/chart metadata. Evaluate two vision-language or code-interpreter models.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Enterprise LLM usage heavily involves structured data analysis. Instruction injection via data metadata is a novel and practically relevant attack surface.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Creating adversarial tables/charts with embedded instructions requires understanding multimodal models and injection techniques. Working with vision-language or code-interpreter models adds complexity. Hard for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 100 tasks is well-defined, but creating convincing injection attacks embedded in structured data requires significant design effort. Moderate scope.

title: Investigating Whether AISafetyLab Evaluations Align with Human Red-Team Findings
original_idea: Run AISafetyLab's automated red-teaming on a model whose human red-team report is publicly available. Compare attack success rates and failure category distributions.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Quantifying the gap between automated and human red-teaming informs how automated evals should be supplemented. Practically important for evaluation methodology.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires setting up AISafetyLab, running automated attacks, and comparing to public red-team reports. Tool setup may have friction, but the analysis is straightforward.

narrow_scope.reasoning: One model, one tool, comparison to one public report. Conceptually narrow, but AISafetyLab setup and ensuring comparable evaluation scope adds work.

title: Benchmark for Evaluating Model Honesty About Its Own Safety Limitations
original_idea: Create 150 prompts at varying distances from clear safety boundaries. Evaluate whether model responses include appropriate epistemic hedging and accurate self-assessment of their safety boundary uncertainty.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Epistemic safety (models honestly flagging uncertainty near safety boundaries) is an underexplored and important dimension. Novel contribution to safety evaluation.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Designing prompts at varying distances from safety boundaries requires nuanced understanding. Evaluating epistemic hedging quality is subjective and hard to automate. Moderate difficulty.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 150 prompts across a spectrum, plus developing evaluation criteria for epistemic hedging. The evaluation criteria design is open-ended. Moderate scope.

title: Investigating Evaluator Anchoring: Does the Order Models Are Presented Affect Safety Rankings?
original_idea: Submit the same model outputs to an LLM judge in randomized orders across ten evaluation runs. Compute whether safety score variance correlates with position in the evaluation queue.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Related to position bias (gen-0666) but for sequential batch evaluation. Incremental extension of known bias. Moderate impact.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Randomize order, run LLM judge ten times, compute statistics. Straightforward experimental design. API calls and basic statistics. Accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Same outputs, ten randomized runs, correlation analysis. Very well-bounded and completable in 30 hours.

title: Replicating Safety Scores Under Decoding Parameter Variation
original_idea: Evaluate two models on HELM Safety at five temperature settings. Compute how safety scores change with temperature and identify hazard categories most sensitive to temperature.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Production deployments use varying temperatures. If safety degrades at higher temperatures, benchmark scores at temperature=0 systematically overestimate deployment safety. Strong practical implication.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Running HELM Safety requires setup of the evaluation framework. Varying temperature is simple but running full benchmark evaluations at five settings for two models is compute-intensive. Moderate complexity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Two models, five temperatures, one benchmark. Clear parametric sweep. Well-defined deliverable. Feasible with medium compute in 30 hours.

title: Benchmark for Safety in Tool-Augmented Retrieval (RAG) Pipelines
original_idea: Construct 120 RAG scenarios where retrieved context contains harmful content. Measure whether the model propagates, qualifies, or refuses the harmful retrieved content across three models.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: RAG is one of the most widely deployed architectures. Safety evaluations ignoring retrieved context leave a major attack surface uncharacterized. Extremely practically relevant.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Setting up RAG pipelines with LangChain/LlamaIndex is documented. Creating harmful retrieved contexts and evaluating model responses is moderately complex. Accessible with medium compute.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 120 scenarios, three models, RAG pipeline setup. Designing harmful retrieved contexts and classification criteria adds scope. Moderate for 30 hours.

title: Investigating Whether Safety Scores Are Consistent Across Inference Frameworks
original_idea: Run the same model on 200 AILuminate prompts through three inference frameworks. Compute disagreement rate in safety scores across frameworks. Identify prompts where framework choice changes the safety verdict.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Relevant reproducibility concern: if safety scores are framework-sensitive, pre-deployment evaluations may not match production. Moderate impact; similar to gen-0682.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires installing and configuring three inference frameworks (HuggingFace, vLLM, llama.cpp). Each has different setup requirements. Moderate complexity for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: One model, 200 prompts, three frameworks. Clear comparison structure. Well-defined deliverable. Feasible in 30 hours if framework setup goes smoothly.
